We’ve got a lot of talent in this locker roo
item.content:encoded:
The Yankees made MLB playoff history in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series, starting eight true left-handed hitters to face right-handed Boston Red Sox starter Sonny Gray.
Never before had a team started that many lefty batters — not including switch-hitters — in a postseason game, per the Elias Sports Bureau.
“I saw our lineup and I assumed that was probably the case,” one of those lefties, Cody Bellinger, told the Daily News with a grin. “I didn’t know. We’ve got a lot of talent in this locker room.”
It was in stark contrast to Tuesday night’s Game 1, when the Yankees started only four left-handed batters against Red Sox lefty Payton Tolle in an eventual 9-0 win in the Bronx.
On Wednesday night, lefty-swinging first baseman Luis García Jr., second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., center fielder Trent Grisham and third baseman Ryan McMahon all returned to the starting lineup as the Yankees sought platoon advantages.
Lefty-hitting Spencer Jones, who started Game 1 in center field, moved to right field for Game 2.
Meanwhile, righty-swinging Paul Goldschmidt, Heliot Ramos, Amed Rosario and Anthony Volpe all began Wednesday’s game on the bench after starting Game 1.
Rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. was the only right-handed batter in Wednesday’s lineup.
Gray is actually a bit tougher against lefty batters than righties, but because the Red Sox carry five left-handed relievers, Boone said he liked having a bench full of right-handed batters that he could deploy in the later innings.
The best-of-three Wild Card Series allows for this kind of maneuvering because, given its short nature, teams are able to carry more hitters and be more aggressive with their bench moves.
The Yankees carried 16 position players in the Wild Card Series, compared to just 10 pitchers.
That likely won’t be the case in future rounds, when they would need to use a fourth starting pitcher and cover more innings with their bullpen.
But Games 1 and 2 against the Red Sox showed how the Yankees plan to approach the postseason, with matchups dictating their lineup decisions perhaps more than they have in the past.
“With this group, I feel like it’s going to take everyone,” manager Aaron Boone said Wednesday. “So that’s my plan — day in and day out, it’s going to be a little different, potentially. And that phrase ‘all hands on deck’ certainly applies to us with our team right now.”
The Yankees need to prioritize lineup creativity even more because the matchup-proof Aaron Judge is sidelined indefinitely with a calf strain.
Giancarlo Stanton — who also typically starts against righties and lefties — is currently relegated to pinch-hitting duty after missing more than five months due to three separate calf strains.
And Wednesday marked the first game started by Grisham since Sept. 4, when he suffered a hamstring strain. After being activated for the Wild Card round, Grisham entered Game 1 in the seventh inning as a defensive replacement and went 0-for-1 at the plate.
“I know he’s ready to go,” Boone said. “I liked his at-bat [in Game 1] when he came in, hit a ball well to center. I don’t know what I’m going to get from any of the guys tonight. But I’ve got a lot of confidence in who he is and what he can bring to the table.”
The Yankees became even more platoon-oriented after they acquired García and Ramos, both of whom perform to traditional splits, before the Aug. 3 trade deadline.
All of those factors led to Wednesday’s historic, lefty-loaded lineup.
“It’s super beneficial for us, because all the guys in the lineup are super tight — righties and lefties — and there will be a lot of different conversations between different guys in what they saw, how they picked it up,” Jones told The News.
“And then we’ve got a bunch of guys ready to go off the bench.”
SCHMIDT SHUT DOWN
Clarke Schmidt’s season is officially over.
The right-hander has been shut down after landing on the IL with right biceps neuritis shortly after making his long-awaited return from Tommy John surgery.
Boone said last week that it was his understanding Schmidt would be shut down, but he hadn’t confirmed it until Wednesday.
But Boone said Schmidt is doing “fine.” That’s in line with what Boone shared last week, when he said Schmidt was expected to have a normal winter to build up for spring training.
More than a year after undergoing elbow surgery, Schmidt made his season debut on Sept. 16 and recorded two outs in a relief appearance.
A starter by trade, Schmidt had hoped to help out of the Yankees’ bullpen this postseason.
But Schmidt experienced a cramping sensation as he warmed up for a second relief appearance, then returned to the IL last Thursday.
VOLPE NEWS
Volpe has a new agent, confirming to The News that he is now being represented by Scott Boras and the Boras Corporation.
Boras is baseball’s most prolific agent, representing stars such as Juan Soto, Gerrit Cole and Bellinger.
Volpe, 25, is eligible for free agency after the 2028 season.

item.content:encoded:
After a Game 1 blowout, the New York Yankees stand poised to finish off the Boston Red Sox in their American League Wild Card Series matchup on Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium.
Sep 29, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; Boston Red Sox outfielder Roman Anthony (19) is introduced before game one of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs against the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images
How to Watch Boston Red Sox vs New York Yankees: Game 2
- Date: Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026
- Time: 8:00 PM ET
- Channel: NBC
The kids led the way for New York in Game 1, with Cam Schlittler allowing just two hits and striking out 10 in 6.1 scoreless innings while Ben Rice banged out two home runs and drove in six on a 4-for-5 night in the Yankees' 9-0 victory. Austin Wells spotted New York to a 1-0 lead with a second-inning RBI single before Rice made it 2-0 with a solo shot to center field in the fifth. Rice drove in a run with a seventh-inning base hit before the Yankees broke things open with a five-run eighth, capped by Rice's grand slam.
The Red Sox, held to three hits, batted just once with a runner in scoring position after Trevor Story's two-out double in the eighth. Starter Payton Tolle took the loss, allowing one run on five hits in 4.2 innings before the bullpen imploded in the late innings.
Left-hander Max Fried goes for the closeout win on Wednesday night for the Yankees. He worked to a 2.80 ERA and 0.994 WHIP in 20 starts and 112.2 innings during the regular season. Right-hander Sonny Gray gets the call for Boston after sharing the MLB lead with 18 wins while posting a 2.72 ERA and 1.148 WHIP in 29 starts and 169 innings. With a win in Game 2, New York heads to Tampa Bay for Game 1 of an AL Division Series on Saturday night.

item.content:encoded:
Segment Spotlight: Quick Hits From Game Time Decisions
Game Expectations with Sonny Gray and Low Scoring Predictions
Sonny Gray is set to take the mound for the Red Sox in a crucial game, bringing his array of five to six well-executed pitches that effectively keep hitters off balance. Despite Gray not being a high strikeout pitcher, his skillset suggests another low-scoring game could be on the horizon.
The previous game's tight scoreline, ending with a narrow win for the Yankees after a strong pitching performance from Cam Schlitler, sets the stage for similar expectations tonight. Doubts linger about the ability of the Red Sox to bounce back offensively after a disappointing display, reinforcing predictions of limited run production in this matchup.
The strategic moves from both teams are pivotal, especially with the Yankees' bullpen showing strength and the Red Sox needing to exploit any opportunity. With Max Fried also not expected to dominate to the extent of Schlitler, the game could hinge on a few critical innings. Tonight's game, with all hands on deck, is anticipated to be a struggle for runs, likely not surpassing a total of 6.5, with potential final scores hovering around 3-2, 4-2, or 5-1.
The outcome of this game could be instrumental in determining the direction of the series, with both teams showing they are prepared to use their top resources to secure a win. However, the prevailing sentiment is skepticism towards a sudden resurgence in offensive performance from the Red Sox, setting up expectations for another tight, low-scoring affair.

item.description: Pat Murphy provided an update on Joey Ortiz as the Milwaukee Brewers prepare for their National League Division Series opener. item.content:encoded:
Pat Murphy provided an update on Joey Ortiz as the Milwaukee Brewers prepare for their National League Division Series opener.
Ortiz underwent an MRI over the weekend, with Murphy saying the structural results were good. However, the Brewers manager remains cautious because Ortiz is dealing with a bruised right knee and abdominal swelling.
Ortiz has not played since leaving Milwaukee's Sept. 25 game against the St. Louis Cardinals in the eighth inning.
Brewers Manager Pat Murphy said Andrew Vaughn is a full go this week, but they are still keeping an eye on Joey Ortiz’s abdomen and knee.
Murphy says Ortiz will be a “little limited” and they are keeping him from some of the higher intensity activities in today’s workout.
The Brewers have extra time to monitor Ortiz because their 103-59 regular season earned them a first-round bye. Milwaukee will open the NLDS on Oct. 3 against the winner of the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres Wild Card Series.
Ortiz was an important part of the Brewers' infield during the regular season. He appeared in 134 games and hit .270 with a .328 on-base percentage, .402 slugging percentage, nine home runs, 47 RBI and nine stolen bases.
Ortiz also recorded 100 hits, 14 doubles and four triples while drawing 35 walks. His availability could give Milwaukee another option in the infield as the team begins its postseason run.
For now, Murphy is giving Ortiz time rather than rushing him back into game action. The seven-day window between his last regular-season appearance and the NLDS gives the Brewers additional time to evaluate his condition.
Milwaukee enters October after winning 103 games, but Ortiz's health is one of the situations the team will continue monitoring before Game 1. His status should become clearer as the Brewers get closer to their postseason opener.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Bryce Harper saves Phillies' season with massive home run vs. Braves after ugly misplay earlier in game
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa
item.description: The duality of Bryce Harper was on full display Wednesday afternoon in Atlanta. In the span of six batters in the seventh inning, Harper badly misplayed a ball in right field that allowed the go-ahead run to cross the plate and hit a game-tying home run as part of back-to-back homers with Kyle Schwarber. Harper also drove in the game's first run with a single in the first inning. He went 2 for 5 in the Phillies' Game 2 win (PHI 4, ATL 3 in 10 innings). "Schwarb, Harp, after we give up those two,
item.content:encoded:
The duality of Bryce Harper was on full display Wednesday afternoon in Atlanta.
In the span of six batters in the seventh inning, Harper badly misplayed a ball in right field that allowed the go-ahead run to cross the plate and hit a game-tying home run as part of back-to-back homers with Kyle Schwarber. Harper also drove in the game's first run with a single in the first inning. He went 2 for 5 in the Phillies' Game 2 win (PHI 4, ATL 3 in 10 innings).
"Schwarb, Harp, after we give up those two, they got momentum," Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. "And to be able to get that back right away was huge."
Philadelphia rearranged its defense to accommodate Luis Arraez at the trade deadline, which pushed Alec Bohm from third base to first base and Harper from first base back to right field. The results were not always positive. On Wednesday, Bohm failed to get an out on a bunt in that seventh inning immediately prior to Harper's misplay. Drake Baldwin lifted a fly ball that Harper misplayed into a double, which gave the Phillies a 2-1 lead.
"Obviously a world of emotion there," Harper said of his misplay. "I didn't think he hit it very hard and I realized he only hit 89 (mph exit velocity), so I thought it was going to be a pop fly just right at me and then it kind of kept traveling. Obviously a ball I should have caught."
Based on the exit velocity and launch angle, Statcast registered Baldwin's double -- "double" -- with an .080 expected batting average. Stats aside, it's a ball that must be caught, much like Ha-Seong Kim's bunt was a ball that had to be turned into an out. Bohm hesitated just enough for Sean Murphy to beat the throw to second base. Little things that cost the Phillies.
"I think it's a ball Bryce probably thinks he should have caught," Mattingly said. "It looked like it kept carrying a little bit. But no, you don't need to say anything to guys like that in that spot, not in this moment."
Matt Olson followed Baldwin's double -- again, "double" -- with a sacrifice fly to give the Braves a 3-1 lead in the seventh inning. The two misplays contributed directly to the two runs. Harper redeemed himself, though. He and Schwarber hit the back-to-back homers in the next half-inning to tie the game 3-3.
Those were the first two home runs Braves setup man Dylan Lee gave up to left-handed batters this season.
"Lee is our high-leverage lefty," Braves manager Walt Weiss said. "Put down the same part of the order yesterday pretty easily. Threw the ball really well yesterday. That's his inning every time."
Bohm redeemed himself as well. After botching the bunt, he hit a go-ahead home run in the top of the tenth inning, which stood up as the game-winning run thanks to Andrew Painter's heroic three-inning relief appearance. The Phillies have pulled even with the Braves in the Wild Card Series. The decisive Game 3 will be played Thursday afternoon.
"There's been a lot of ups and downs," Bohm said about his season. "Didn't start the best. I don't really know how to put it all into words quickly, but it's just been a long road with a lot of ups and downs. I've learned a lot, and I've made a lot of really close friends along the way and had a lot of people to lean on along the way. I really wouldn't have rather had it any other way."
To make the infield work with Arraez, the Phillies shifted Bryson Stott from second base to third, Bohm from third base to first, and Harper from first base to right. Prior to Arraez's arrival, Harper had not played the outfield since 2022. He moved to first base that summer to limit his throwing following his return from Tommy John surgery.
Arraez rolled his ankle at the end of the regular season and is not on the Wild Card Series roster. His status for the rest of the postseason, should the Phillies advance, is up in the air.

item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball announced today that it has approved a roster substitution for the Boston Red Sox due to an injury sustained by outfielder Roman Anthony. As a result, Anthony will be replaced by Curtis Mead on Boston’s roster vs. New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie. Dr. Gary Green, MLB’s Medical Director, confirmed the injury after a full review of the medical information.
MLB Postseason rules provide that a Club may request permission from the Commissioner’s Office to replace a player who is unable to play because of an injury. The Commissioner’s Office may approve or disapprove the request based on the specific facts and circumstances. In accordance with the rules, Anthony will be ineligible to return in the American League Division Series presented by Booking.com if the Red Sox participate, but he would be eligible to return for the American League Championship Series if Boston qualifies.
The Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie will be broadcast by NBC, Peacock and NBC Sports Network while ESPN Radio provides live national coverage. MLB Network will air extensive studio coverage throughout the Postseason across the Emmy Award-winning MLB Tonight, the Emmy-nominated MLB Central and MLB Now, and Intentional Talk, MLB Network’s longest-running talk show. Postseason games throughout 2026 will also be telecast in Spanish on Universo and Univision, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. The 2026 Postseason will be distributed by MLB media rightsholders in 16 different languages to fans in more than 200 countries and territories.

item.title: [lanacion.com.ar] Thin MLB crowds in Atlanta, Houston show challenge of selling afternoon Wild Card Series tickets
item.description: Thin MLB crowds in Atlanta, Houston show challenge of selling afternoon Wild Card Series tickets A late home run secured a playoff win for Atlanta; stadium attendance remains low for scheduled weekday afternoon games - 1 minuto de lectura' Austin Riley delivered the first clutch moment of Major League Baseball's playoffs on Tuesday, hitting a go-ahead three-run homer in the eighth inning that pushed the Atlanta Braves over the Philadelphia Phillies for a 5-3 win . It was an electric scene for fa
item.content:encoded:
Thin MLB crowds in Atlanta, Houston show challenge of selling afternoon Wild Card Series tickets
A late home run secured a playoff win for Atlanta; stadium attendance remains low for scheduled weekday afternoon games
- 1 minuto de lectura'
Austin Riley delivered the first clutch moment of Major League Baseball's playoffs on Tuesday, hitting a go-ahead three-run homer in the eighth inning that pushed the Atlanta Braves over the Philadelphia Phillies for a 5-3 win .
It was an electric scene for fans at Truist Park — at least for those who decided to show up.
There has been a noticeable number of empty seats in Atlanta and Houston for day games during this week's Wild Card Series, with the Braves drawing 30,127 fans for Game 1 on Tuesday that started at 2 p.m. local time, well below the 41,108 capacity. The Astros announced that 34,011 fans attended Tuesday's 4 p.m. Game 1 at Daikin Park, also well below its 41,168-seat limit.
It's not the first time this has happened.
Since MLB permanently expanded the playoffs to a 12-team bracket in 2022, just six of 26 afternoon Wild Card Series games through Tuesday have reached or exceeded stadium capacity. Seven games failed to reach even 85% capacity. The Braves-Phillies game on Tuesday was 73.2% full, which is the lowest since the postseason expanded, according to research from Sportradar.
Game 2 of the Braves-Phillies series had an announced crowd of 37,150 on Wednesday.
The main issue for day games is obvious: It's hard for fans to attend day games during the week — particularly in late September and October — because people have to work and children are back in school. It doesn't help that those game times are announced with only a few days' notice.
Still, it's a less-than-ideal atmosphere for some of the most important contests of the year.
Phillies third baseman Alec Bohm shrugged off the smaller crowds before Wednesday's game, saying his team just wants to win games and advance.
“I don’t think anybody on our team is really focused on how many people are showing up here," Bohm said. "It’s just kind of -- I think, like you said, it’s a 2 o’clock game in the middle of the week, so I think that might have something to do with it.
“That doesn’t take away from what’s going on on the field and kind of the stakes of all that in our minds.”
All three ALWCS games in Cleveland last year between the Guardians and Detroit Tigers started at 1:08 p.m., and none drew more than 30,000 fans. The Tampa Bay Rays had just 19,704 for an ALWCS opener against Texas in 2023 that started at 3:08 p.m., the lowest attendance for a non-COVID MLB postseason game since the 1919 World Series.
MLB declined to comment on the attendance numbers, but the league spreads its wild-card games throughout the day on purpose so they have their own television window and capture the largest viewing audience possible. NBC is paying the league roughly $200 million per year to host “Sunday Night Baseball” and the Wild Card Series during a three-year deal agreed to last November.
The Astros fans who did attend Tuesday's game were in a bit of a foul mood, peppering the team with boos as they fell behind 5-0 by the fifth inning on the way to a 6-3 loss. Astros manager Joe Espada said he understood the fans' frustration but hoped for a better atmosphere on Wednesday.
“I do want our fans to know that we love them and we need them,” Espada said. “They’re part of what we are trying to accomplish here. They’re part of our family.”
AP Sports Writers Charles Odum in Atlanta and Kristie Rieken in Houston contributed to this story.
See AP’s full MLB coverage here

item.content:encoded:
Philadelphia Phillies right fielder Bryce Harper made a crucial mistake in Game 2 of the National League Wild Card Series against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park.
With runners on first and second base and one out in the bottom of the seventh inning, Braves DH Drake Baldwin hit a deep fly ball to right field. Harper misplayed the ball, allowing Baldwin to reach on a double and a run to score, giving Atlanta a 2-1 lead.
The Braves added another run in the inning on a sacrifice fly from Matt Olson.
If the Phillies lose today, they will be eliminated from the postseason. If they come back, there will be a Game 3 tomorrow.

@MattGelb: With the season in the balance, Bryce Harper misplays a ball in right field that is scored a double. The Phillies’ defense has hurt them all season; a fitting way for this to perhaps end. Cris Sánchez threw a career-high 116 pitches.

The MLB Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie begins on Tuesday, and all games in this round will be available exclusively on NBC platforms.
Each series will be a best of three, meaning there will be four games on Tuesday, another four games on Wednesday and up to four games on Thursday depending on how many series go the distance.
As you prepare for what will be a thrilling postseason, here’s what you need to know to make sure you are ready to tune in from the jump.
Quick guide to watching the Wild Card Series on NBC and Peacock
- Wild Card games will be available this year on NBC platforms.
- All Wild Card games will be available on Peacock Premium or Premium Plus (descriptions available here).
- Peacock is available across a variety of devices. To get started, find or download the Peacock application on your device or head directly to PeacockTV.com to create a Peacock account.
- For questions on how to sign up and access via your device you can reference Peacock's Getting Started Page.
- Games available on NBC broadcast will also be available on Peacock.
- Games that are not available on NBC broadcast will be available on Peacock and also on NBC Sports Network (NBCSN).

NBC and MLB go way back
NBC has a long history with MLB. The first MLB broadcast on TV was a 1939 Cincinnati Reds-Brooklyn Dodgers doubleheader on W2XBS (the precursor to WNBC-TV) in New York. NBC Sports was the home to the first World Series broadcast in 1947, the first All-Star Game nationally broadcast in 1952 and has televised 39 World Series -- more than any other network.
From 1957-2000, NBC Sports was home to a wealth of baseball programming, including Game of the Week and Monday Night Baseball telecasts, more than 30 All-Star Games and countless iconic postseason moments. MLB Sunday Leadoff -- a first-of-its-kind Sunday morning presentation featuring a unique three-announcer broadcast booth with one analyst with expertise on each team joining play-by-play voice Jason Benetti -- returned to NBC and Peacock this season after previously airing on Peacock during the 2022-23 seasons.

item.title: [heavy.com] Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 3 Sudden Roster Moves Amid MLB Playoffs
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: The MLB playoffs are in full swing, as Wild Card matchups began this week. For the Los Angeles Dodgers, they are still awaiting their opponent for the NLDS. It will be either the Atlanta Braves or the Philadelphia Phillies. Amid the MLB playoffs, the Dodgers made a few roster moves in preparation for their upcoming series. More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Tyler Mahle News After Dramatic Phillies Game Los Angeles Dodgers Make 3 Roster Changes The Dodgers do know that they will begin the
item.content:encoded:
The MLB playoffs are in full swing, as Wild Card matchups began this week.
For the Los Angeles Dodgers, they are still awaiting their opponent for the NLDS. It will be either the Atlanta Braves or the Philadelphia Phillies.
Amid the MLB playoffs, the Dodgers made a few roster moves in preparation for their upcoming series.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Announce Tyler Mahle News After Dramatic Phillies Game
Los Angeles Dodgers Make 3 Roster Changes
The Dodgers do know that they will begin their quest for a three-peat on Saturday, October 3.
In the meantime, here are the three roster moves the team made, per the team’s transactions tracker:
“Los Angeles Dodgers activated RHP Edgardo Henriquez from the 15-day injured list.”
“Los Angeles Dodgers recalled LHP Ronan Kopp from Oklahoma City Comets.”
“Los Angeles Dodgers recalled SS Hyeseong Kim from Oklahoma City Comets.”
The most notable roster move of the trio is Edgardo Henriquez being activated from the 15-day IL, which could be a huge boost to the Dodgers’ bullpen. However, he still needs to be announced on the Dodgers’ NLDS roster, which has not been made public yet.
As for Hyeseong Kim, he could be a pinch-runner option if the Dodgers opt to go that route.
More MLB on Heavy: Chicago Cubs Announce Interesting Seiya Suzuki Decision Before MLB Playoffs
What Do Roster Moves Mean for Los Angeles Dodgers Playoff Chances?
If Henriquez can go for the Los Angeles Dodgers’ relief corps, that is a huge boost because he has been one of the team’s breakout pitchers and a highly dependable reliever.
As for the other two moves, they might not be noticeable now, but could play a role down the line.
Ronan Kopp being recalled to the 40-man roster is likely in case of an emergency, but if the Dodgers advance past the NLDS, there’s a slight chance he could be added to the official postseason roster.
Hyeseong Kim is a player who could pay slight dividends on the bases if manager Dave Roberts opts to use him in the late innings as a pinch-runner option.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Edwin Diaz Committed to "Earning" Spot on Postseason Roster
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Edwin Díaz knows exactly what is at stake over the final days of the regular season. After an injury-plagued year and an uneven return to the majors, the veteran reliever is trying to convince the Dodgers that he belongs in their postseason bullpen. Saturday brought another encouraging step in that direction. Díaz worked a scoreless inning against the Giants and, more importantly, came away feeling that the fastball command that had eluded him earlier in the season is finally b
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Edwin Díaz knows exactly what is at stake over the final days of the regular season.
After an injury-plagued year and an uneven return to the majors, the veteran reliever is trying to convince the Dodgers that he belongs in their postseason bullpen. Saturday brought another encouraging step in that direction.
Díaz worked a scoreless inning against the Giants and, more importantly, came away feeling that the fastball command that had eluded him earlier in the season is finally back.
“Yeah, 100%,” Díaz said when asked if he feels better now than he did before his latest stint in Triple-A. “I’ve been able to throw strikes. I think that was my problem, my concern. I wasn’t throwing my fastball for strikes. Now I’m able to command my fastball really good. And when I command my fastball, my slider plays up.”
That relationship between the two pitches is critical for Díaz. When the fastball is located properly, hitters have a much tougher time distinguishing it from his slider before the breaking ball dives away.
“Right now it’s really good,” Díaz said of the slider. “It’s going down and away. I’ve been able to throw my fastball glove side, so if I throw my fastball glove side, the slider will play off the same path.”
Díaz believes the improvement traces back to a mechanical adjustment made during his time at Oklahoma City.
Following a rough Triple-A appearance, he sat down with the pitching coaches and identified an issue with his hip movement and posture. He said the correction also helped restore an arm slot that had drifted earlier in the season.
“We found I wasn’t moving my hips the right way,” Díaz said. “We started working on that. On Tuesday I threw a really good pen. On Wednesday I pitched, I felt great, and lately I’ve been really good.”
The Dodgers have also been able to ease Díaz back into major league competition without immediately asking him to protect one-run leads in the ninth inning. He said he is perfectly comfortable with that arrangement.
“I’m open-minded right here,” Díaz said. “I need to help this team win. Whatever Doc puts me in the game, in any situation, I will do my job. I feel good. I just want to keep climbing the ladder and finish the season strong.”
That ladder could eventually lead to an October roster spot, but Díaz knows nothing has been guaranteed.
Dave Roberts has acknowledged that there is competition for the final places in a crowded Dodgers bullpen, and Díaz understands that his performance over these final games matters.
“I got to show them that I’m part of that bullpen,” Díaz said. “I haven’t pitched this year, and when I’ve been in the majors, I’ve been struggling. So right now I’m giving my 200% just to show them I will be in that roster spot.”
For Díaz, the path from here is simple: keep throwing strikes, keep getting clean innings, and give the Dodgers a reason to trust him in October.
“Every time they give me the ball, in any situation, I will do my job,” he said. “And then at the end of the season, they will make decisions.”
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves are one win away from a trip to the National League Division Series and a date with the back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers. They fell into an early 1-0 hole against the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 2 of the NL wild card series, but that didn't stop star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. from doing something special that has only been done twice in Braves history.
With the Braves down 1-0, Acuna stole two bases in the bottom of the first inning and ultimately scoring the team's first run on Matt Olson's RBI single to tie the game up. According to Sarah Langs of MLB.com, Acuna has joined two Braves legends on an all-exclusive list.
Ronald Acuna Jr. makes Braves history
Acuna has also become the seventh player in postseason history with two stolen bases in the first inning of a game. That was last done by Phillies star shortstop Trea Turner in Game 2 of the NL Division Series against the New York Mets.
But it still has been a very long time since a member of the Braves accomplished this feat. Rafael Furcal was last with the Braves in 2005, so it has been over two decades since a Braves player has pulled this off.
Acuna is a former MVP, NL Rookie of the Year, three-time Silver Slugger and five-time All-Star. He is signed through this season and has club options for 2027 and 2028.
During the regular season, the 28-year-old outfielder hit .255/.345/.451 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 21 stolen bases and a .796 OPS. Injuries limited him to 107 games, but he has started the postseason off with a bang and is a big reason why the Braves are now pointed towards the NLDS.
But along with his power and solid defense has come some elite speed and baserunning, and he put that on full display in Game 2 as the Braves punched back from an early deficit against the Phillies and put themselves in position to potentially advance to the next round.
The postseason is always full of historic moments, and Acuna created one of his own with his speed on the basepaths. It will be interesting to see if the Braves can ultimately take Game 2 and effectively end the Phillies' season. A win advances them to the next round.
The game is currently tied at one apiece in the fourth inning.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. Curt’s work includes covering trade and free agency predictions, as well as rumors and news. item.title: [MLB.com] Pivetta tabbed to start Game 2 after missing most of 2026 with right elbow injury
item.dc:creator: Cole Bradley
item.description: SAN DIEGO -- Through Nick Pivetta’s first four starts this season, it was clear he was picking up right where he left off from his career-best 2025 campaign, one that saw him finish sixth in National League Cy Young Award voting … only for it to be derailed by a right elbow injury in April that cost him nearly five months. item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO -- Through Nick Pivetta’s first four starts this season, it was clear he was picking up right where he left off from his career-best 2025 campaign, one that saw him finish sixth in National League Cy Young Award voting … only for it to be derailed by a right elbow injury in April that cost him nearly five months.
But upon his return on Sept. 7, Pivetta reassumed the version of himself that was prevalent throughout last year, putting a lengthy rehab behind him and leaving no doubt that he was fully ready to contribute on the biggest stage.
This time, though, he’ll have the Petco Park crowd behind him.
“We're very lucky to have such a great fan base here,” Pivetta said. “From what I've heard from the guys that have played here before, I'm expecting great things and very excited for it. Just trying to keep all my focus on the game, but enjoy those moments, too, with those fans and try to bring the championship home for them.”
Since returning from the injured list, Pivetta has looked a lot like the guy who posted a 2.87 ERA across 31 starts in ‘25. He allowed a mere three runs over 18 2/3 innings over four starts, good for a 1.45 ERA. He delivered 4 2/3 scoreless frames against the Dodgers in Los Angeles his last time out, helping the Padres secure their third consecutive trip to the postseason that night.
“High level of confidence with Nick, what a road he’s been on this year,” Padres manager Craig Stammen said. “For him, when it didn’t look great at the beginning of the season, to put in the work over an entire season and not know if he’s ever going to get back … now he’s [been] one of our best pitchers down the stretch.”
The four-start runway Pivetta had allowed him to build up to full pitch count (he threw 87 pitches in his last start), meaning there should be zero limitations for him this postseason.
Of course, the Padres almost certainly won’t need him to go a full four or five innings, given their elite bullpen that was pieced together specifically to help shorten games in the playoffs -- a formula that San Diego has deployed with great success in its previous seasons and seems poised to do once more.
But Pivetta’s postseason track record is nothing to scoff at.
He was brilliant for the Red Sox during their playoff run in 2021 that saw him come out of the bullpen in the American League Division Series against the Rays before he twirled five innings of one-run ball against the eventual World Series champion Astros in Game 4 of the AL Championship Series. And, of course, he held the Cubs to just two runs over five innings and struck out nine in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series last year, capping off an excellent first season in San Diego.
That Chicago lineup will be a little different this time -- much stronger, for one. He’ll have to navigate a top of the order that includes the likely NL MVP in center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and a surging Alex Bregman, who posted a 1.010 OPS in the second half.
“It's a whole lineup; they make good contact, they don't swing outside of the zone,” Pivetta said. “They have guys in there that jell really well together, led by Bregman. It's just trying to keep them off-balance, but always sticking to my strengths and doing what I do best and just see where that night goes.”
Pivetta is up for the challenge.
“I'm healthy, I'm feeling good and I'm excited for the next step,” he said.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have yet to begin their quest for a three-peat during these MLB playoffs, which are already underway, but on paper, LA is going to be a tough out regardless of its opponent.
However, even though the MLB playoffs are underway, it’s not too early to start thinking about the major offseason decision the team faces regarding ace starter Tarik Skubal.
Recently, in an MLB free agent predictions piece, Tarik Skubal is being linked back to the Los Angeles Dodgers on a 10-year deal.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 3 Sudden Roster Moves Amid MLB Playoffs
Dodgers Predicted to Retain Tarik Skubal
Back in August, the Dodgers shocked the MLB world by landing Tarik Skubal in a huge trade with the Detroit Tigers.
However, they (LA) face a big decision regarding his free-agent status, as he is set to hit the open market after the 2026 season.
BleacherReport.com’s Zach Buckley recently predicted LA to retain its new ace via a 10-year deal:
“Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Dodgers on a 10-year deal.”
“In short, the crystal ball sees this coming down to the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets—two of the biggest spenders in baseball. The Dodgers just made an aggressive move for Skubal at this year’s trade deadline, while the Mets badly need a boost to their rotation. This bidding war should be ferocious, but in the end, the Dodgers’ head start by having Skubal already on the roster could be what pushes them over the edge.”
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to Austin Riley Moment in Phillies-Braves Game
Tarik Skubal Has Proved His Worth with Los Angeles
Let’s be clear: the 2X AL Cy Young winner in Tarik Skubal, doesn’t have to prove his worth to anybody, but since joining the Dodgers, he’s made it really hard for the team to ignore that he would be an immense addition to the starting rotation.
Across 10 starts with LA, Skubal holds a 2.61 ERA with 70 strikeouts.
He will be a huge piece to the Dodgers postseason fold, and if he really helps propel LA to a three-peat, that might be enough to truly force Andrew Friedman’s hand in his ongoing contract talks.
Dodgers fans, do you want to bring back Tarik Skubal? And at what price would you be willing to do so?

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Pete Crow-Armstrong’s Card Sells for $1.1 Million Before Cubs Elimination Game
item.dc:creator: Erik C Anderson
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong's historic season just produced another staggering number, this time away from the baseball field. The Chicago Cubs star's one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.098 million at Goldin. The PSA Gem Mint 10 card, which also received a PSA 10 autograph grade, features the MLB Debut patch from Crow-Armstrong's first major-league game on September 11, 2023. It is a massive sale by itself. The timing makes it even more striking. Crow-Armstrong jus
item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong's historic season just produced another staggering number, this time away from the baseball field.
The Chicago Cubs star's one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.098 million at Goldin.
The PSA Gem Mint 10 card, which also received a PSA 10 autograph grade, features the MLB Debut patch from Crow-Armstrong's first major-league game on September 11, 2023.
It is a massive sale by itself.
The timing makes it even more striking.
Crow-Armstrong just completed a historic 40-home run, 40-stolen base season and helped Chicago reach the postseason. Now, only days later, his signature rookie card has approached the MLB Debut Patch record while Crow-Armstrong and the Cubs enter an elimination game against the San Diego Padres.
$1,098,000: Winning bid for Pete Crow-Armstrong’s debut patch jersey tonight at @GoldinCo.
PCA’s 2024 rookie salary: $740,000. pic.twitter.com/d21WopsNpx
— Darren Rovell (@darrenrovell) September 30, 2026
Pete Crow-Armstrong Card Sells for $1.098 Million
Crow-Armstrong's card was one of the most significant MLB Debut Patch cards to reach the market since Paul Skenes' one-of-one sold in 2025.
Goldin listed the card as Crow-Armstrong's 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph 1/1, graded PSA Gem Mint 10 with a PSA/DNA Gem Mint 10 autograph grade.
The $1.098 million result also produced a remarkable comparison highlighted by Rovell.
Crow-Armstrong earned roughly $740,000 during the 2024 season, meaning a collector just paid considerably more for his one-of-one rookie card than the Cubs paid Crow-Armstrong to play an entire major-league season.
But the final auction price may be even more notable for what it narrowly failed to accomplish.
Pete Crow-Armstrong Falls $12,000 Short of Paul Skenes Record
Crow-Armstrong came extraordinarily close to taking down the benchmark for MLB Debut Patch cards.
Skenes' one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.11 million through Fanatics Collect in March 2025. The price included the buyer's premium and established the Skenes card as the highest-selling MLB Debut Patch at the time.
Crow-Armstrong finished at $1.098 million.
The difference?
Just $12,000.
That puts Crow-Armstrong and Skenes in remarkably similar territory despite playing dramatically different positions and arriving in the majors with different levels of prospect hype.
Skenes was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 MLB Draft and won National League Rookie of the Year in his first season. His Debut Patch became a national story even before it surfaced, with the Pittsburgh Pirates famously offering the young collector who pulled it a package that included 30 years of season tickets.
Crow-Armstrong's card reached seven figures after a different catalyst: one of the greatest individual seasons ever produced by a Cubs player.
Pete Crow-Armstrong Made Cubs History Before $1.1 Million Sale
The auction could hardly have closed at a better moment for Crow-Armstrong's hobby profile.
On September 24, Crow-Armstrong stole his 40th base of the season, joining the exclusive 40-40 club after already reaching 45 home runs.
He became just the seventh player in MLB history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in the same season. He also became the first Cubs player to accomplish the feat.
And he did it on the same night Chicago clinched an NL Wild Card berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins.
Crow-Armstrong entered the postseason hitting .280 with 45 home runs and 107 RBIs while appearing in all 159 Cubs games through the clinching victory.
That transformed the timing of the Goldin auction.
Collectors were not merely bidding on the Debut Patch of a promising young Cubs player.
They were bidding on the Debut Patch of a 24-year-old who had just completed the first 40-40 season in franchise history.
Now the attention shifts back to what Crow-Armstrong can do on the field.
Cubs Face Elimination Against Padres After 8-0 Loss
Chicago enters Game 2 of its Wild Card Series against San Diego needing a victory to keep its season alive.
The Padres routed the Cubs 8-0 in Game 1 on September 29.
San Diego starter Michael King took a no-hit bid into the seventh inning and ultimately allowed only one hit over seven scoreless frames while striking out eight. Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts each homered for the Padres.
The Cubs will send Kevin Gausman to the mound for Game 2 opposite Nick Pivetta
There is at least one reason for optimism surrounding Crow-Armstrong specifically.
Chicago dominated San Diego during the regular season, winning five of six games and outscoring the Padres 55-28.
Crow-Armstrong was one of the Cubs' biggest problems for San Diego.
He hit .364 with four home runs in the six regular-season meetings.
Chicago will need another performance like that now.
Crow-Armstrong has already produced one of the defining baseball-card sales of 2026 and one of the most statistically significant seasons in Cubs history.
Whether his week is remembered primarily for a $1.098 million card sale or for what happens in October now depends on what Crow-Armstrong and the Cubs do next.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Pete Crow-Armstrong's Card Sells for $1.1 Million Before Cubs Elimination Game appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [fansided.com] 5 free agent landing spots for Michael King after sterling playoff start
item.dc:creator: Christopher Kline

Plenty of Padres deserve credit for Tuesday night's dominant performance, but none more than soon-to-be-free agent Michael King. item.content:encoded:
The San Diego Padres blitzed the Chicago Cubs in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card series, 8-0, to put themselves one win away from a date with the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLDS. Plenty of Padres deserve credit for Tuesday night's dominant performance, but none more than soon-to-be-free agent Michael King.
San Diego's ace put together one of the best postseason starts in recent memory, carrying a no-hitter into the seventh inning. He finished with seven scoreless frames, allowing one hit, three walks and recording eight strikeouts. As Padres fans celebrate King's masterclass, prospective free agency suitors are chomping at the bit. Here are a few potential landing spots:
Atlanta Braves
The Braves rotation is a bit scarce behind Chris Sale. Tyler Mahle has eviscerated the competition since arriving at the trade deadline, but he's a free agent next winter. AJ Smith-Shawver, J.R. Ritchie and Owen Murphy are all exciting young arms, but it's unclear which of them will click as full-time starters — and how soon. Martín Pérez, one of this season's great surprises for Atlanta, is also an upcoming free agent.
Atlanta doesn't typically pay sticker price on free agent pitchers but there is immense pressure to compete now — right now — in the twilight years of Sale's career. He won't be able to anchor this rotation forever and the Braves need to start hedging their bets, just in case Father Time catches up.
King, with a 3.21 ERA and 1.18 WHIP, has made 32 starts and pitched a career-high 185 innings this season. The Braves need depth and dependability most desperately, and that's something King can provide. It doesn't hurt that he is building a nice postseason résumé for himself.
Baltimore Orioles
Every winter, we all wonder if Baltimore might finally upgrade its pitching staff. The Corbin Burnes era burned bright and fast. Shane Baz was a savvy trade addition last winter, but the Orioles still struggled to field five quality, healthy starters for the 162-game duration of the regular season.
Trevor Rogers, their best pitcher two years running, will now enter free agency. That leaves Baltimore's front office will a clear and immediate need in the rotation. It seems like the O's new ownership group will, on some level, spend more than the previous administration. The Pete Alonso signing was a stark departure from business as usual in Baltimore. As such, it's not hard to envision the O's ponying up for a second-tier ace like Michael King; the Tarik Skubals of the world are still outside their price range, no doubt.
If Kyle Bradish can finally get healthy for a year, and if the O's deign to re-sign Rogers (or pursue another mid-rotation arm in addition to King), this rotation could shape up quite nicely. Baltimore has the offensive firepower to compete in the AL East. King can help round out a postseason-caliber roster.
Toronto Blue Jays
A nightmare Blue Jays season has finally come to an end, but Toronto should be right back in the postseason fray next season with better luck and an productive winter. The Jays front office is probably the most aggressive in baseball outside of L.A. or New York.
Last offseason, their big fish was Dylan Cease, who immediately turned in a Cy Young-caliber campaign. At the trade deadline, Toronto did not strictly sell, despite sitting near the bottom of the standings. The Jays went out and added José Soriano, another frontline starter at the peak of his powers.
Toronto can expect a healtheir Trey Yesavage in 2027, too, so a premium free agent addition (like King) could quickly transform the Blue Jays rotation into one of the deepest and most fearsome in the American League. If Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Toronto's boppers put their best foot forward, there's no reason Toronto can't win the division and compete (again) for a World Series.
Houston Astros
The Astros went bullpen against bullpen in their AL Wild Card series opener against the White Sox. Houston was lucky Chicago only managed six runs, with many, many base-runners stranded in scoring position. That did not mean much for the Astros, unfortunately, as the Chicago bullpen — against all odds — mostly kept a more seasoned Houston lineup in check.
Houston has a proper 1A ace in Hunter Brown, but the rotation behind him is total patchwork. Peter Lambert put together a solid campaign and Ethan Pecko faired well in his first taste of MLB action, but the Astros can't really trust anyone besides Brown. Tatsuya Imai, their prized free agent addition last winter, was little more than a bulk reliever in his rookie season.
The Astros have gotten cheaper and cheaper in recent years and the results are getting worse and worse, predictably. Still, this core has competed for a World Series in the not-so-distant past, and we know ownership is capable of spending at the upper echelon of free agency. King would do a lot to solidify the Astros' pitching plans in 2027.
Chicago Cubs
Injuries decimated the Cubs rotation this season. Justin Steele, Cade Horton and Ben Brown should all return in 2027, which is a major, natural influx of talent. If Edward Cabrera can rebound, the Cubs rotation will be all rainbows and sunshine — at least on paper.
But as this season once again reminded us, what happens "on paper" almost never translates to reality. Shōta Imanaga and Matthew Boyd are both upcoming free agents. Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes, Chicago's emergency deadline rentals, are also halfway out the door. There's uncertainty around how exactly the likes of Steele and Horton will perform coming off of major elbow surgeries, too. So the Cubs should play it safe and hyper-focus on pitching depth.
The rotation could be what sends Chicago home against San Diego. So, why not use the Padres own weapons against them in free agency and sign King? "Stability" is a word that comes to mind with King, and that's exactly what the Cubs need right now.

item.description: Kyle Tucker is a four-time All-Star and one of the best outfielders in baseball when healthy. item.content:encoded:
Kyle Tucker is a four-time All-Star and one of the best outfielders in baseball when healthy.
His production during the 2026 regular season was not on par with what he accomplished earlier in his career.
This year was Tucker's first with the Los Angeles Dodgers. They likely imagined him as another superstar in a lineup that includes Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, and Freddie Freeman.
Unfortunately for the Dodgers, Tucker's offensive game took a significant step back.
"Well, the Dodgers could still three-peat, but it hasn't been a very impressive first season in Los Angeles for Tucker," Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly wrote.
Tucker played in 154 games and hit just 17 home runs, looking completely lost in right field at times.
"After signing a four-year, $240 million contract that includes a player opt-out after the second season, Tucker has produced just a 98 OPS+ in 2026," Kelly added. "Mind you, 100 is considered a league-average player, and Tucker averaged a 142 OPS+ from 2020-2025."
How can Tucker win back the trust of Dodgers fans?
MORE: Pirates urged to re-sign Brandon Lowe if they ‘want to be taken seriously’
A strong postseason would be an excellent starting point.
"Tucker is finishing the season on a high note, as he has a .921 OPS in September. If he has a big October, no one will remember how much he struggled during the regular season," Kelly wrote. "But this has definitely been an underwhelming campaign for the four-time All-Star."
The Dodgers are a threat to win a third consecutive championship. If Tucker can carry his success from September to October, Los Angeles will be very hard to dethrone.

item.title: [heavy.com] When is Luis Arraez Coming Back? Injury Return Timeline for Phillies' Second Baseman
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies traded for Luis Arraez to make their lineup deeper when they reached the MLB playoffs. But now in the postseason, and facing elimination on Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves, the Phillies don’t even have Arraez available to play for them. It’s an unfortunate reality, and it’s one the Phillies are going to have to navigate if they want to see Arraez put on their uniform again. The Phillies lost the NL Wild Card Series opener on Tuesday to the Braves when Austin Riley
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies traded for Luis Arraez to make their lineup deeper when they reached the MLB playoffs.
But now in the postseason, and facing elimination on Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves, the Phillies don’t even have Arraez available to play for them.
It’s an unfortunate reality, and it’s one the Phillies are going to have to navigate if they want to see Arraez put on their uniform again.
The Phillies lost the NL Wild Card Series opener on Tuesday to the Braves when Austin Riley hit a go-ahead home run for Atlanta in the eighth inning.
In a best-of-three series, it’s Wednesday or bust for the Phillies.
Arraez will only be able to watch and hope he gets another chance before Philadelphia’s season is over.
And given that Arraez’s contract expires after this season, he may never play for the Phillies again if they lose on Wednesday.
When is Luis Arraez Coming Back?
There’s no real clarity on Arraez’s return timeline yet.
The veteran sprained his left ankle on Thursday, Sept. 24, while running on the bases. He went down in a lot of pain and had to essentially be carried off the field.
The Phillies left him off of the NL Wild Card Series roster. Otto Kemp, a utility player with a great old-school baseball name, is on the roster for this series in Arraez’s place.
“We still get improvement every day, but not enough,” Mattingly told reporters on Monday about Arraez. “He was going to try to hit today and just wasn’t able to do it. So, we kind of crossed that bridge today.”
Arraez hadn’t swung a bat yet as of the time Mattingly spoke to reporters on Monday.
The contact wizard was also seen with a boot on his foot during the Phillies’ celebrations on Sunday after they clinched a playoff spot.
Arraez won’t be eligible to play against the Braves in the Wild Card Series since he was left off the roster.
That means that he can only play if the Phillies win the best-of-three series in Atlanta.
At that point, the Phillies would get the chance to name a Divisional Series roster. Players can be swapped in and out then, which would allow Arraez back into the mix if he’s ready.
Luis Arraez Stats
Arraez has been solid since coming to Philadelphia. He’s batted .278 with 10 doubles, two home runs and 21 RBI in 46 games.
He had been hitting .324 with the Giants before the trade.
He’s also made major strides as a second base defensive player in 2026, going from a negative there to a clear positive — although a sprained ankle might not help.
Arraez had settled into the cleanup spot for the Phillies — a very new-age decision to put the best contact hitter on the team at the 4-spot in the batting order. It was mostly working, though, and Philadelphia has to win without Arraez to give him another chance to get back in the lineup.

item.description: It’s do or die for the Phillies on Wednesday. The Braves pushed them to the brink in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card with a 5-3 decision prompted by Austin Riley’s three-run shot in the eighth inning. Another win in this series would mark first time the Braves prevailed over their NL East rivals in the postseason: the Phillies took the NLDS in both 2022 and 2023 and the 1993 NLCS over Atlanta. item.content:encoded:
It’s do or die for the Phillies on Wednesday.
The Braves pushed them to the brink in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card with a 5-3 decision prompted by Austin Riley’s three-run shot in the eighth inning.
Another win in this series would mark first time the Braves prevailed over their NL East rivals in the postseason: the Phillies took the NLDS in both 2022 and 2023 and the 1993 NLCS over Atlanta.
This Phillies’ core has been chasing after a World Series throughout the decade, and another early exit will have its ramifications.
The onus to avoid that comes down to no one more than Bryce Harper, who struck out twice and went hitless Tuesday.
Phillies vs. Braves Game 2 prediction, best bet
Harper, who is a .269 postseason hitter in 58 games, narrowly missed a go-ahead two-run home run against Chris Sale in the sixth inning when the ball just sailed just right of the right-field pole.
He gets the lefty vs. righty matchup advantage against Atlanta’s Tyler Mahle, against whom he has posted a healthy .278/.350/.500 slash line.
Mahle leans on his four-seamer for nearly half of his pitches. He doesn’t throw it with extreme movement or overpowering velocity, averaging 92 mph, but he locates the strike zone with it well.
In the 14 four-seamers that Mahle served to Harper this season, Harper knocked two hits with a home run on eight swings, according to Statcast. Only two were whiffs.
In fact, Mahle wasn’t much of a swing-and-miss pitcher at all, ranking in only the 31 percentile.
That’s all while Harper remained an elite contact hitter, posting a .379 xwOBA, a Statcast metric that measures expected offensive production based on the exit velocity and launch angle of his contact rather than the results.
Harper has stated he loves playing at Truist Park, and his numbers say why.

The two-time MVP hit .320 there in 27 plate appearances this season, which included a pair of home runs and five multi-base games out of six.
As the clubhouse leader, Harper was adamant about how the Phillies need to “finish the job” this postseason after having been here before.
He’ll have no choice but to deliver on that statement Wednesday.

item.title: [fansided.com] Roman Anthony injury update: Do Red Sox have a chance without young star?
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: Boston Red Sox fans entered Game 1 of the Wild Card Series on Tuesday night with cautious optimism. They hoped to avenge last year's crushing loss against Massachusetts native Cam Schlittler by beating him up this time around, with their ace, Payton Tolle, on the mound, and their star outfielder, Roman Anthony, in the leadoff spot. Well, Tolle was fine, but Schlittler was dominant, the New York Yankees won convincingly, and, as if that wasn't bad enough, Anthony left the game in the sixth inning
item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox fans entered Game 1 of the Wild Card Series on Tuesday night with cautious optimism. They hoped to avenge last year's crushing loss against Massachusetts native Cam Schlittler by beating him up this time around, with their ace, Payton Tolle, on the mound, and their star outfielder, Roman Anthony, in the leadoff spot.
Well, Tolle was fine, but Schlittler was dominant, the New York Yankees won convincingly, and, as if that wasn't bad enough, Anthony left the game in the sixth inning for a pinch-hitter. So to sum up, the Red Sox are down in this best-of-three series one game to none, and could be without their young star with their season on the line on Wednesday. Not great!
Roman Anthony injury update brings worst case of deja vu to Red Sox fans
Anthony missed more than three months on the Injured List with a right wrist injury. The Red Sox were able to rebound following an atrocious start without him, somehow, but obviously missed him dearly when he was out. Sure enough, the injury Anthony suffered on Tuesday was an aggravation of the ailment that kept him out for roughly half the year, according to manager Chad Tracy.
When asked whether Anthony will play on Wednesday, all he said was, "We'll have to see what tomorrow brings." That does not sound encouraging for a Red Sox team whose season is officially on the line.
As frustrating as this injury is, it's a bit less shocking that it occurred, knowing that he appeared to have tweaked it on an awkward swing in Sunday's game. What's particularly irritating is that Sunday's game was completely meaningless for both Boston and the Cubs, their opponent. Anthony did not have to play, but did, and might've ended his season in the process.
He might play, but Anthony struck out in each of his first two at-bats of Tuesday's game, and who knows if he's close to healthy. This is not good news for Boston, and neither is their projected lineup for Game 2 without him.
Projected Red Sox lineup without Roman Anthony shows they're in trouble
| Player | Position |
|---|---|
| 1. Jahmai Jones | DH |
| 2. Adley Rutschman | C |
| 3. Willson Contreras | 1B |
| 4. Wilyer Abreu | RF |
| 5. Ceddanne Rafaela | CF |
| 6. Nick Sogard | 2B |
| 7. Trevor Story | SS |
| 8. Caleb Durbin | 3B |
| 9. Jarren Duran | LF |
There's some talent here. Jahmai Jones has crushed left-handed pitching since arriving with the Red Sox, so perhaps he can set the tone in Anthony's place against left-hander Max Fried on Wednesday. Guys like Adley Rutschman, Willson Contreras, Wilyer Abreu and even Ceddanne Rafaela are capable of doing damage at all times. Hey, even Trevor Story doubled on Tuesday for Boston's only extra-base hit.
With that being said, though, the Red Sox looked rather punchless at the plate all of Tuesday's game. I know Schlittler started it, but one extra-base hit in a playoff game is pretty pathetic. That was with Anthony playing in half the contest. Can the Red Sox score runs against Fried, who is also elite, by the way, without Anthony? It's hard to believe that, especially with how this offense has looked in September.
Red Sox season feels finished after Game 1 gut punch
It'd be foolish to count out any postseason team, especially one like the Red Sox, who went on a 32-5 run this season. They've proven they can bounce back from adversity, and if they can just find a way to win Game 2, suddenly they'd be one win away from eliminating the Yankees and advancing to the ALDS.
Still, only one team has won Game 1 of a Wild Card Series and gone on to lose that best-of-three affair since MLB made the permanent switch to that format in 2022. That team? The Boston Red Sox, who blew a 1-0 series lead to these Yankees in the Bronx. The circumstances were different, though. The Yankees were the home team, they still had Aaron Judge healthy, and they didn't lose 9-0 the night before.
I don't want to count Boston out, but even getting to Game 3 has been challenging for teams that drop Game 1 of the Wild Card series. The Red Sox have their work cut out for them, especially if Anthony has to miss time and/or is at all compromised due to his wrist injury, which, at this point, feels likely.

item.title: [Chicago Tribune] The best advice young Chicago White Sox players received in their 1st postseason
item.dc:creator: LaMond Pope
item.description: HOUSTON — Chicago White Sox pitcher Sean Burke sat next to designated hitter Andrew Benintendi during the flight to Houston ahead of the American League wild-card series. “Kind of just talked about playoffs, his past experiences, some stuff that we need to do,” Burke said on Tuesday afternoon at Daikin Park. “His advice was just kind of keep doing what we’ve been doing the whole year.” That’s the approach the Sox took into the postseason. Several players are experiencing the playoffs for the fir
item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON — Chicago White Sox pitcher Sean Burke sat next to designated hitter Andrew Benintendi during the flight to Houston ahead of the American League wild-card series.
“Kind of just talked about playoffs, his past experiences, some stuff that we need to do,” Burke said on Tuesday afternoon at Daikin Park. “His advice was just kind of keep doing what we’ve been doing the whole year.”
That’s the approach the Sox took into the postseason. Several players are experiencing the playoffs for the first time. That includes Burke, who is in line to pitch in some role in Game 2 against the Houston Astros on Wednesday.
“I don’t think really anything needs to change,” Burke said. “We got here for a reason, and we know we have a good team, we have a talented group. I think just focusing on playing our brand of baseball is going to be good enough for us.”
Benintendi was the only White Sox player in Tuesday’s starting lineup with major-league playoff experience. He played in the postseason in 2016-18 with the Boston Red Sox. The 2018 club won the World Series.
“It’s always nice to make the playoffs,” Benintendi said on Sunday. “I haven’t played in any since 2018. I was with the Yankees, but I was hurt during their run in ’22.
“It’s exciting. It’s always fun. At the least, it’s an experience for everyone in here to dip their toes in it.”
Benintendi is one of the players shortstop Colson Montgomery leaned on.
“If you look at our lineup, it consists of a lot of kind of rookies and guys who this is our first full year,” Montgomery said before Tuesday’s game. “But also, we have a lot of veterans that have been in this scenario. (Outfielders Tommy Pham), (Benintendi), (Randal Grichuk), those guys have definitely been the people we’ve leaned on.
“And they just go out there and they’re telling us, try to make it seem like it’s another game. Go about your routines the exact same because once the game starts, it’s the same thing we’ve been playing 162 games. It can be more magnified. You can make it feel that way, but it’s just kind of the stuff they have been telling us is just take it day by day and just be you.”
Montgomery said it was important not to overanalyze the situation.
“I just feel like when you’re young and you’re hungry and you’re competitive and you’re in a scenario like this, it’s kind of like one of those things where you go out there and play,” he said. “You go out there and you compete. You don’t overanalyze a lot of things. You kind of just go out there and do what you know, and that’s play baseball. We’ve all been playing baseball for our whole lives, so in our eyes this is something that’s not anything different.
“But we’re all excited. All the young guys, we’re all pumped to be here.”
While the team did receive a special letter from Pope Leo XIV, manager Will Venable didn’t feel a special speech was necessary.
“These guys have a full understanding of what this is, even if they haven’t been here before,” Venable said on Tuesday. “We’ve talked about some of the environments and situations that we played in, especially in the second half of this year, going to Wrigley (Field to play the Cubs), going to Yankee Stadium (to play the New York Yankees), whatever it might be, and playing in those high-leverage moments and experiencing that.
“Of course, there’s nothing like the playoffs and, that’s going to be a different beast all in itself and they will have to experience that for themselves. There’s nothing that I can say that can help them feel what it’s going to feel like.”

item.title: [MLB.com] Riley flips Game 1 with 8th-inning blast on 99.9 mph pitch from Phillies' closer
item.dc:creator: Mark Bowman
item.description: ATLANTA -- Austin Riley supported Chris Sale’s strong start, halted the Phillies’ postseason dominance of Atlanta and put six months of frustration behind him with a swing that could make October worth savoring for both him and the Braves. Riley’s three-run homer off All-Star closer Jhoan Duran with two outs in the eighth inning gave the Braves a thrilling 5-3 win over the Phillies in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series on Tuesday afternoon at Truist Park. “I’m happy for Austin Riley,
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- Austin Riley supported Chris Sale’s strong start, halted the Phillies’ postseason dominance of Atlanta and put six months of frustration behind him with a swing that could make October worth savoring for both him and the Braves.
Riley’s three-run homer off All-Star closer Jhoan Duran with two outs in the eighth inning gave the Braves a thrilling 5-3 win over the Phillies in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series on Tuesday afternoon at Truist Park.
“I’m happy for Austin Riley,” Braves manager Walt Weiss said. “It’s been a tough year for him. But this just goes to show you, when the playoffs start, everything starts at zero. Nothing that happened in the regular season really matters. It’s a clean slate. Austin Riley has been a great postseason player.”
Four of Riley’s six career postseason homers have been of the go-ahead variety and three of those have been hit in the eighth inning or later. That eighth inning or later total matches Troy Glaus, Bernie Williams, Jose Altuve and Freddie Freeman for the most in MLB history.
The slugging third baseman previously hit a go-ahead shot in the ninth inning of Game 1 of the NLCS on Oct. 12, 2020, and he hit a go-ahead two-run home run with two outs in the bottom of the eighth in Game 2 of the 2023 NLDS, also against the Phillies. Chipper Jones is the only other Braves player with multiple go-ahead homers in the eighth inning or later of a postseason game.
“I know how my season went,” Riley said. “It’s not the way I wanted it to. But that's the beauty of the postseason. You get a clean slate and go out there and try to do something for the boys and for this city.”
Instead of talking about being on the brink of elimination, the Braves joyfully discussed how everything changed when Riley sent Duran’s 99.9 mph fastball over the right-center-field fence for a go-ahead home run.
Riley doesn’t remember what any of his teammates said after he returned to a jubilant dugout after his home run. Was he also in a haze as he rounded the bases?
“I remember my gum falling out of my mouth,” Riley said.
It was a jaw-dropping moment that put the Braves in an encouraging position.
In the history of the best-of-three Wild Card Series, teams taking a 1-0 lead have gone on to win the series 21 of 24 times (88%), including 17 two-game sweeps. Home teams have won all nine series in which they have gone ahead 1-0, including eight sweeps.
The Phillies had won six of the previous eight postseason games played against the Braves this decade. Philadelphia beat Atlanta in the 2022 and ‘23 NL Division Series.
“It doesn't get more fun than this, playing this game in the postseason,” Weiss said. “You can imagine going from losing the lead to something like that. The swinging emotions are enormous. What a big home run.”
Sale played a significant role in this crucial Game 1 victory. The Braves ace registered nine strikeouts over 6 1/3 innings. Two of the three runs he surrendered came via a J.T. Realmuto triple that Didier Fuentes surrendered with two outs in the seventh.
So where was Sale when the value of his strong effort was preserved by Riley’s home run?
“I was getting some arm care in, and unfortunately the [clubhouse] TV I was watching was on the delay [feed],” he said. “I just heard craziness coming from the entire clubhouse. Everyone's losing their mind, and I'm just sitting there like, ‘Oh, what's going on?’ About four seconds later, you see what happened. I just couldn't be happier for him.”
Coming off two injury-shortened seasons, Riley hit .219 with 19 homers and a .654 OPS during the regular season. Safe to say this was the most frustrating season of the two-time All-Star’s career. This past weekend in Miami, he talked about how relaxing his right shoulder might have helped him hit two homers in last week’s Reds series.
The triple came against a 98.2 mph splitter that was in the middle of the zone. The ball had 109 mph exit velocity and it traveled a Statcast-projected 394 feet.
This home run came against a 99.9 mph four-seamer that was middle in. This is the hardest-thrown pitch Riley has homered against in his career, besting a homer he hit against Jacob deGrom’s 99.7 mph heater on July 1, 2021.
This latest home run had a 104.6 mph exit velocity and it traveled a projected 385 feet.
It would have been a home run in 27 of 30 MLB ballparks. Did Riley know it was gone?
“No, I did not,” he said. “I was just praying as I was running to first.”

item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club
24-year-old Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong joined one of the rarest clubs in Major League Baseball this season. The NL MVP favorite became the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 40+ bases in a single season.
While there are only a select few talented players who have made the club, there are several players from this generation who have made the cut and also invented clubs of their own.
Here is a list of the 7 players to make the 40/40 club:
RELATED | Top 20 All-Time Greatest Baseball Players
RELATED | MLB Players Who Played In The Little League World Series
1988 Jose Canseco – 42 HR, 40 SB, .307 AVG, .391 OBP, .569 SLG
The founding member of this club, Canseco, predicted he would achieve this milestone. He also drove in a league-leading 124 runs and posted a heavy .569 slugging percentage to coast to a unanimous AL MVP.
Canseco would lose to the Dodgers 4-1 in the World Series, winning the only game with a grand
1996 Barry Bonds – 42 HR, 40 SB, .308 AVG, .461 OBP, .615 SLG
Bonds paired pure athleticism with legendary plate discipline, combining 42 home runs and 40 stolen bases with a career-high 151 walks.
His absurd .461 OBP ensured he was constantly on base to leverage his speed, though his 9.7 WAR effort incredibly finished fifth in a hitter-dominated NL MVP vote that season.
Even with Bonds’ historic run, the Giant’s struggled this season, finishing 68-94 and 4th in the NL West.
1998 Alex Rodriguez – 42 HR, 46 SB, .310 AVG, .360 OBP, .560 SLG
At just 22 years old, A-Rod accomplished what remains the most physically demanding 40/40 season by doing it as a everyday shortstop.
He recorded an MLB-leading 213 hits, which helped him finish the season with a 43.9 Power/Speed number—the highest mark ever achieved in baseball history.
Rodriguez’s Mariners failed to reach the playoffs as well, ending the season at 76-85 and 3rd in the AL West.
2006 Alfonso Soriano – 46 HR, 41 SB, .277 AVG, .351 OBP, .560 SLG
After coming just one home run short with the Yankees in 2002, Soriano left no doubt during his single, explosive season in Washington.
He blasted 46 home runs and swiped 41 bags. Soriano’s season stands out unique because he also hit 41 doubles, creating the game’s only 40/40/40 performance.
The Nationals also failed to reach the postseason, finishing 71-91 and 5th in the NL East.
2023 Ronald Acuna Jr. – 41 HR, 73 SB, .337 AVG, .416 OBP, .596 SLG
Acuña weaponized MLB’s larger bases and rules limiting pitcher disengagements to turn the 40/40 club completely on its head.
While maintaining a career-best .337 batting average, he bashed 41 home runs and ran wild for 73 stolen bases, easily taking home NL MVP honors.
After Acuna’s record-breaking season, the superstar struggled in the postseason, hitting 2-14 and only scoring two runs. The Braves would fall in the NLDS to the Philadelphia Phillies.
2024 Shohei Ohtani – 54 HR, 59 SB, .310 AVG, .390 OBP, .646 SLG
Serving strictly as a designated hitter while rehabbing his throwing arm, Ohtani reached 40/40 in a blistering 126 games—shattering Soriano’s previous speed record of 147 games. He hit a walk-off grand slam to secure the milestone, eventually pushing his totals to 54 home runs and 59 steals to create the 50/50 club.
Ohtani is the only player so far to cap off his historic season winning the World Series, beating the Yankees in 5 games.
2026 Pete Crow-Armstrong – 45 HR, 41 SB, .280 AVG, .372 OBP, .570 SLG
Originally known as a spectacular, defense-first center fielder, PCA shocked the baseball world by developing top-tier power to accompany his elite speed. He tied for the MLB lead with 45 home runs and secured his 40th stolen base during the Cubs’ playoff-clinching victory in late September.
The Chicago Cubs will play in the Wild Card round on Tuesday.
Who do you think had the most impressive season? Let us know!

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the 2026 MLB playoffs, baseball fans. The postseason got started Tuesday with a quartet of Game 1s in the best-of-three Wild Card Series. The Braves came back against the Phillies in the early start, while the White Sox cruised to an easy win against the Astros and . In the late slate, Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning en route to a blowout Padres win over the Cubs.
In these short series, the Game 1 winners are one victory away from the LDS round, and the Game 1 losers are one loss away from their season being over.
The Rays, Guardians, Brewers and Dodgers all secured byes and await the winners in the next round. The Rays are the American League's top seed and will face a division rival in the ALDS, whether it's the Yankees or the Red Sox. The Guardians, despite an 85-77 record that ranks 10th out of the 12 playoff teams, earned the No. 2 seed in the AL and will face either the 84-win White Sox or 81-win Astros in the next round.
The Brewers (103 wins) and Dodgers (100 wins) both hit triple digits in the win column in the regular season, and they will host NLDS Game 1s on Saturday. The Brewers get the Padres-Cubs winner, while the two-time reigning champion Dodgers get either the Braves or the Phillies.
Below is a look at the full 2026 MLB playoff bracket and the playoff schedule.
